implementation.owner_boundary: Environment owns claim operation identities, lifecycle events, and retry reconciliation; Store continues to own immutable claim persistence and generation compare-and-swap.
request_protocol: Bind claim acquire, release, and transfer request IDs to canonical payload digests.
Return the original result for an exact retry and reject a reused request ID with changed effect or provenance payload.
Publish one atomic release/recipient pair for transfer and validate both records before reporting a retry as committed.
Record request-bound no-op releases so a later claim cannot be released by replaying a request that already completed as a no-op.
Deduplicate the Environment release event when Store claim publication succeeded but the caller snapshot save was interrupted.
store_invariants: Claim mutations continue through Store claim batches with expected-generation CAS.
Immutable claim history and exact transfer provenance are preserved.
No direct canonical Store filesystem access, alternate persistence database, or persistence fallback was added.

environment_vertical_proof.summary: provider bindings, protected write denial, checkpoint, fresh-process resume, handoff, and completion

scoped_static_checks.ruff_select: E4,E7,E9,F passed on changed Python modules and tests

new_regression_coverage: Acquire/release/transfer request IDs reject changed payloads and accept exact retries.
Interrupted session snapshot save after Store claim release reconciles without duplicating the release event.
A completed no-op release request cannot affect a claim acquired later.

limitations: This change hardens Environment claim request replay and release reconciliation; it is not evidence that every legacy request record has an original payload digest.
Canonical Store publication and the protected execution transport are evidenced separately in the existing Control acceptance record.
